S1.why: Short adjective after the count; 'gratis' is the word every free slot uses across the sheet.

S2.why: An invitation in tú imperative, the way the vocabulary file already addresses the person; no limit word, no sales verb.

S3.s: Tus %lld cutlings gratis ya están en uso. Nunca te costarán nada y seguirán funcionando.
S3.back: Your %lld cutlings free already are in use. Never to-you they-will-cost nothing and they-will-keep working.
S3.why: This folder may be read in Spain or across Latin America, so 'ya están en uso' avoids choosing between 'has usado' and 'usaste'.

S4.why: Plain statement of what is open to them; lowercase 'cutlings' in running text, as the vocab's iCloud sentence writes it.

S5.why: 'Llevas X de Y' is how both Spain and Mexico say progress so far; order matches the variables, so no positional forms needed.

S6.why: Fits 24 with '5.000' or '5,000'; 'espacio para' would run over and needs the noun anyway.

S7.why: Uses the vocab's Texto and Imágenes as the two kinds; tú imperative.

S8.why: Spanish list: commas, 'y' before the last, no serial comma.

S9.s: Una compra sirve para todos tus dispositivos con tu cuenta de Apple.
S9.back: One purchase serves for all your devices with your account of Apple.
S9.why: 'cuenta de Apple' lowercase as the vocab writes it; 'sirve para' is neutral in every region.

S10.why: 'una sola vez' stresses once without the commercial 'pago único'; second person keeps the warmth.

S11.s: Sin suscripción, sin anuncios y sin registrarte.
S11.back: Without subscription, without ads and without registering-yourself.
S11.why: Three real things, so three items; 'registrarte' is the everyday verb for creating an account.

S12.why: The exact label Spanish-language iOS apps use for the App Store restore action, in every region.

S13.why: Gerund of S12 with the single ellipsis character.

S14.why: Infinitive, as iOS Spanish buttons are; S10 already says once, so the capsule stays short beside a long price like '79.000 Rp'.

S15.why: Same infinitive without the price, 11 characters.

S16.why: What iOS Spanish dialogs say to put something off; it postpones without refusing.

S17.why: The verb iOS uses on close buttons in Spanish.

S18.why: 'esto' points at the grid of room that just filled the sheet; warm, tú, no exclamation.

S19.s: Gracias por tu compra. Apoyas a Cutling y a la única persona que lo hace.
S19.back: Thanks for your purchase. You-support to Cutling and to the only person who it makes.
S19.why: 'la única persona que lo hace' says one maker plainly; Cutling stays a name and takes 'lo' (masculine).

S20.s: Hola de nuevo. Tu compra ya está restaurada.
S20.back: Hello again. Your purchase already is restored.
S20.why: Neutral greeting with no gender and no regional idiom.

S21.why: 'en uso' avoids picking a past tense, so it is spoken the same in every region.

S22.why: The bare number at the end works for 1, 2, 5 and 21 with no plural noun after it; positional forms because the room comes first.

S23.why: Past participle agrees with the name Cutling (masculine); 'caben' is the natural verb for room.

S24.s: No se pudo completar la compra
S24.back: Not itself could complete the purchase
S24.why: 'No se pudo' is said the same in Spain and Latin America, so it suits the shared folder; 30 characters.

S25.s: No se puede conectar con el App Store en este momento. Inténtalo de nuevo en un rato.
S25.back: Not itself can connect with the App Store in this moment. Try-it again in a while.
S25.why: 'En este momento' and 'inténtalo de nuevo en un rato' read natural on both sides of the Atlantic.

S26.s: El App Store no ha confirmado esta compra.
S26.back: The App Store not has confirmed this purchase.
S26.why: The perfect is standard in written Spanish everywhere for a result that still matters; S24 already uses 'no se pudo'.

S27.s: La cuenta de Apple de este dispositivo no tiene compras anteriores de Cutling.
S27.back: The account of Apple of this device not has purchases earlier of Cutling.
S27.why: States the fact about the account, no blame; 'dispositivo' covers iPhone and iPad.

S28.s: La versión gratis guarda %lld cutlings. Desbloquea Cutling una vez y guarda todos los que quieras.
S28.back: The version free saves %lld cutlings. Unlock Cutling one time and save all those that you-want.
S28.why: 'gratis' after the noun, as everywhere else in the app; 'todos los que quieras' is the spoken 'as many as you like'.

S29.why: Compact pair with 'gratis', 13 characters at 4 of 5.

K1.why: The preterite is grammatical in every region and is the only form that fits 38; the perfect runs over.

M2.why: M1 plus the ellipsis character because it opens a window.

M3.why: Row label in the list title's capitalised form, with the app's 'gratis'.

M5.why: Masculine participle agrees with the name Cutling.

M6.s: Una sola compra desbloquea Cutling en iPhone, iPad y Mac.
M6.back: One single purchase unlocks Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: Same list form as S8; 'una sola' carries 'once'.

M7.s: Desbloqueado en iPhone, iPad y Mac con esta cuenta de Apple.
M7.back: Unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac with this account of Apple.
M7.why: Participle agrees with Cutling from the row above; vocab's 'cuenta de Apple'.

M8.s: Compraste Cutling antes de que fuera gratis, así que sigue desbloqueado. Gracias por tu apoyo.
